text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bourse watchdog STE slashes Amsterdam Stock Exchange's supervision. (p1)
- Rabobank and ING Bank raise long-term mortgage rates by 0.4 percent. (p1)
- Profit growth of bank insurance group Fortis supercedes expectations. (p1)
- Textile group Van Heek-Ten Cate plans bourse launch before 2000. (p1)
- Smit Transformatoren books 1.1 million guilders 1996 net compared with 47.1 million guilders losses in 1995. (p3)
- Automation company Multihouse announces a change in its corparate strategy. (p3)
- Bank insurer ING's realty arm ING Vastgoed takes 50 pct stake in shopping mall in Lisbon. (p15)
- Realty fund VIB reckons with limited profit growth. (p15)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Investment group Robeco does not give a forecast about the direction of the stock exchanges. (p2)
- Secondment and services firm Goudsmit takes over Belgian rival Edora. (p2)
- Dutch people are sceptical about firms connecting their name with charitable causes, appears from research. (p2)
- Fortis is to thoroughly reorganise its foreign currency unit GWK. (p31)9
DE TELEGRAAF
- ABN Amro bank no longer wants "coffeeshops" selling softdrugs as clients. (p1)
- Telephone rates in the Netherlands are among the lowest in Europe --- survey of 14 countries. (p10)
- Rotterdam-based bulk transhipment group HES Beheer's solvancy very weak after mega losses in 1996. (p21)
- Electronics producer Nedap is to split its shares 1:4.
TROUW
- Cut price airliner EasyJet's complaint about Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM's price dumping seems valid. (p7)
- Engineering bureau Fugro sees growing chances in Hongkong. (p22)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma considers the privatisation of Amsterdam Schiphol Airport possible and advisable. (p1)
- Automation companies Baan and Oracle fight for order to modernise ABN Amro bank's foreign transactions system. (p11) --Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
